title: Adaptive allocator thaw + evictor-thermostat to stop long-tail GPU OOMs from KV growth
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private reported periodic GPU OOM crashes that occur only after long-lived sessions (6+ hours) with mixed chat/embedding workloads. Symptoms: sudden spike in resident GPU memory used by runtime arena, followed by kernel OOM and host-side process crash. Incidents observed in three tenants (one Dedicated, two Hosted) with high prefix-KV churn. This ticket contains the investigation summary, proposed runtime patch, rollout plan, and follow-up actions for stability and observability improvements.
investigation_summary: Reproduced on internal stress harness by running high-rate chat traffic with repeated prefix updates and session pinning. Heap profiling and KV index traces showed the KV index growing with tombstone accumulation and small live fragments that prevented slab coalescing. The allocator kept handing out many small allocations which increased arena fragmentation; background compaction was starved under sustained request concurrency. Additionally, an async prefetch path was creating ephemeral handles that deferred cleanup to a slow background worker which fell behind under peak load, increasing live set size.
root_cause: (1) Fragmentation from many small ephemeral allocations combined with deferred tombstone reclamation in the KV index. (2) Background compactor/backoff wasn't keeping up because it relied on single-threaded periodic pass. (3) Under heavy tail traffic the allocator refused to trigger proactive thaw/defragmentation which allowed resident GPU memory to climb until OOM. Race between prefetch handles and eviction path left soft references preventing eviction.
solution_summary: Ship a runtime patch that implements: (A) an "evictor-thermostat" that monitors slab free ratio and triggers graded eviction+compaction actions; (B) allocator thaw path that opportunistically coalesces adjacent free slabs during low-request windows; (C) defensive KV-index delta checksum reconciliation to drop stale tombstones earlier; (D) backpressure on async prefetch when compactor lag exceeds threshold. The changes are designed to be safe on-hosted and in air-gapped Private environments and are feature-flagged for staged rollout.
implementation_notes:
- Added meters: slab_free_ratio, compactor_lag_ms, kv_tombstone_rate, prefetch_queue_depth.
- Evictor-thermostat runs in the runtime's maintenance thread; on violation it ramps eviction aggressiveness in three steps (gentle, moderate, aggressive) and can engage a paused-defrag mode.
- Allocator thaw performs cooperative coalescing limited by budgeted GPU cycles to avoid latency spikes.
- Prefetch path now exposes reservation handles that honor immediate cancellation; if compactor_lag > 2000ms prefetch is rate-limited.
- All new code gated under runtime-evictor-thermostat FF and exposed via control-plane rollout flags for Dedicated and Private.
- Added unit + stress tests: slab-coalesce property tests, tombstone GC unit, and 24h soak harness scenario replicating tenant workload.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind FF and feature flag enabled in CI. 2) Deploy canary to internal staging with targeted chaos workload for 48h. 3) Enable FF for non-critical hosted canaries (5% traffic) for 24h, monitor metrics. 4) Enable for affected Dedicated tenant in maintenance window and observe for 72h. 5) Gradual ramp to 50% hosted, then 100% if stable. 6) For Private customers, provide patch bundle and runbook for controlled upgrade; default FF off unless explicitly enabled.
rollback_plan: Revert feature flag to disable evictor-thermostat and thaw path. Runtime supports hot-disable: new maintenance cycles will stop eviction ramp and prefetch rate-limits. If memory pressure persists after toggle, revert the runtime revision to previous stable release and run manual GC compaction steps described in runbook.
qa_steps:
- Run perf/stability soak with 8-12 concurrent long-lived sessions for 48h and verify slab_free_ratio stays above safety threshold.
- Validate that aggressive eviction step reduces resident memory without causing request error rates > 0.1%.
- Confirm prefetch rate-limit prevents compactor_lag from growing under simulated spike.
- Run upgrade/rollback test: enable FF, then disable and ensure state returns to baseline without leaked references.
- Verify unit tests and stress harness pass in CI and on staging canaries.
